done_criteria: Row may move to DONE only when persistence+validation+authorization+branch scope+business logic+workflow+accounting/stock effects+notifications+audit+UI+error handling are connected end-to-end AND its listed tests pass. Menu/route/button/table existence is never DONE.
decisions: D1..D24 as defined in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 0
global_invariants: one company per operational instance (no multi-company in tenant ERP)
normal printed sales document titled INVOICE; tax section only when applicable; Mushak 9.1/11 separate document types
double-entry: sum(debits)=sum(credits) on every posted journal
stock truth = immutable stock movements; balances derived/rebuildable
approval engine generic and data-driven (no per-module hardcoded approval logic)
no external AI API dependency; recommendations explainable and non-authoritative
notifications truthful provider states; no fake sent
audit append-only with actor/action detail; created_at is not an audit system
exactly 25 dashboard widget containers (Branch Comparison + Recent Activity combined)
public tokens opaque, hashed, revocable/rotatable, rate-limited
salary acknowledgement persisted in database (survives refresh/logout/login/restart)
tool/technician requisitions never become customer invoice lines
warranty activates idempotently from actual delivery event only

01_dashboard.notes: All 25 containers (decision D22) are answered by one read service, App\Domain\Dashboard\Services\DashboardMetrics: each container resolves to ok (a figure from the company's own documents), empty (source exists, no rows yet) or unavailable (the source does not exist yet and the panel names the module that will fill it - 01-21 expiry is the live example). Nothing is estimated and no panel carries a fixture. Visibility is the module's own view permission (DashboardMetrics::PERMISSIONS), so a user who may not read invoices never sees invoice totals; GET /app/dashboard/widgets/{code} refuses the same containers the page hides. Reuses CustomerQuery::dueBuckets, PurchaseQuery::payablesAgeing/receiptsByDay, ReorderService::alertRows and LeaderboardQuery so a panel cannot disagree with the screen it links to. Deviations from the planned per-widget controllers/registry and dashboard.widget.* keys are recorded in the traceability file. Fixes a real defect: WidgetSeeder produced mixed-case container codes (Todays_Sales) while translations (widget.todays_sales), label keys and the dashboard metric map all key off lowercase slugs - codes are lowercase now and the seeder prunes containers outside the catalogue. 01-27 stays PARTIAL: the widget admin CRUD belongs to 12 Settings, still PLANNED.

03_purchase.notes: Purchasing core + purchase bills. Suppliers (03-01/02/04), purchase orders with server-derived totals and a two-permission approval (03-22/23/24), receipt-state facets (03-25), PO→GRN with a hard over-receipt guard (03-29), goods receipts as the only inbound stock path with idempotent postings and valuation at cost paid (03-32/33/36), batch capture (03-34), and bills: entry from a posted receipt or direct (03-45), payable created by approval (03-44/03-46), three-way match (PO↔GRN↔bill) computed, stored and displayed (03-50), supplier payables with ageing buckets (03-48 partial). Approval posts a real journal entry through posting_rules seeded by PurchaseCoreSeeder (Dr inventory 1140 for goods-backed bills or Purchases & Services 5225 for direct ones, Dr input tax 2120, Cr accounts payable 2110); the maker can never approve their own bill. Partial: contacts/bank/TIN on one record (03-05), fixed category vocabulary (03-06), payment terms without a schedule (03-11), spend without scoring (03-12), no outbox so no 'sent to supplier' state (03-24), KPIs without report routes (03-31), ageing without a report screen (03-48). Not started by design: purchase requests, amendments, print/outbox, bill payment recording/print/reports (03-47/49/51), supplier payments (03-52…03-58), returns (03-59…03-64), RFQ, import/LC and the report family. Approval uses the direct permission purchase.bills.approve / purchase.orders.approve, not the Workflow engine, and a three-way mismatch is recorded rather than blocked (no configurable tolerance yet). Supplier payments (03-47, 03-52) reuse the shared payments table (direction out, supplier_id) and the polymorphic payment_allocations rows: SupplierPaymentService refuses an unposted or settled bill, refuses more than the balance, returns the original payment for a repeated idempotency key, posts Dr Accounts Payable 2110 / Cr Cash in Hand 1110 or Bank Account 1120 through posting_rules (supplier_payment / supplier_payment_bank), and moves paid_amount / due_amount / status on the bill inside the same transaction. Payment history filters by voucher, supplier, method, date and the bill it settled. Advances (03-53), BEFTN (03-54), schedule (03-55), payment approval workflow (03-56), reminders (03-57) and report exports (03-58) are still missing, as are purchase returns and debit notes (03-59…03-64) — the only honest correction path for a posted receipt or bill. Purchase returns (03-59, 03-60, 03-61) close the loop: a return is raised from a posted receipt (lines prefilled with received / already returned / returnable), from an open bill (service or goods with no receipt on file) or standalone, and quantities are capped at received − already returned, so the same goods cannot be claimed twice. Approval moves stock out through PURCHASE_RETURN_OUT (stock-managed products only, idempotent per line) and posts the debit note through posting_rules: purchase_return_posted (Dr AP 2110, Cr Inventory 1140, Cr Tax Payable 2120) or purchase_return_expense_posted (Cr Purchases & Services 5225). When the return names a bill, the same transaction credits it through a new credited_amount column, so due = total − paid − credited and the bill's own balance keeps agreeing with accounts payable; a credit larger than the bill's outstanding balance is refused rather than becoming an unapplied debit note (03-63). Posted returns are immutable; only unposted ones can be cancelled, with a reason. Still missing: return shipment tracking (03-62), the GL-derived supplier ledger and statement (03-63/06-08/06-14), report exports (03-64), supplier advances/BEFTN/schedule (03-53…03-57). Bill ageing (03-48) is now a screen of its own: GET /app/purchase/payables groups every open bill by supplier with current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+ columns from each bill's own due date (an undated bill is never late), a totals row and bucket filters, and the supplier profile and ledger show the same buckets for one supplier. Returns appear as credits in the supplier's account (03-63 partial) and are capped at the bill they correct.

04_inventory.notes: Reading half of stock, plus the damage & loss family. Alerts: ReorderService::alertRows() judges each product against the policy that governs it in that warehouse (a warehouse row beats the company-wide row); a product with no active policy is deliberately never listed. A damage entry (04-46) moves goods into the damaged compartment with no valuation effect - reversible with a release; a loss entry (04-47) consumes the layers and posts Dr Inventory Loss & Damage 5260 / Cr Inventory 1140 through the stock_loss_posted rule; a write-off (04-48) is the document that removes value, raised against a compartment and approved by a second person (self-approval refused in the service), restating each line to the cost the ledger actually consumed; 04-49 values every statement from stock_layers, never an estimate; 04-51 reports the cost by kind/cause/warehouse/month with the damaged compartment valued at what a write-off would remove. The ledger state machine moved to StockMovement::applyDelta() - one definition shared by post, rebuild and the ledger view - and an outbound move from the damaged compartment no longer decrements on_hand a second time. 04-50 (insurance claims) stays PLANNED: it needs an insurance register nothing else in the system carries. 04-31 (stock count / cycle count) is built: a sheet snapshots the balance each line is asked about, counting is blind for anyone who cannot post, posting makes the counted figure the truth for the counted lines (the delta is measured against stock now, not the snapshot, so movement during the count is visible rather than smoothed) and writes the difference as one stock adjustment through PostStockAdjustment::post — the same path a manual adjustment takes. An uncounted line is left alone, a cancelled sheet corrects nothing and a posted sheet is closed. Posting carries its own permission (inventory.counts.post) because counting and changing the books are different jobs. 04-28 (transfer approval) is built on the same shape as 04-26 and with a stricter consequence: an approved transfer becomes a *draft*, so the two-leg lifecycle is untouched and a waiting transfer cannot be dispatched at all — the gate is a refusal in `dispatch()`, not a hidden button. Threshold `inventory.transfer_approval_above` (default 0), value frozen in `total_value` (a line with no cost is valued at source cost), maker ≠ checker, rejection terminal and needing a reason, audits transfer_submitted/approved/rejected. 04-26 (adjustment approval and history) is built: the approval lives on the document rather than in a generic request table, the threshold comes from the inventory settings (default 0 = everything posts as before), a document at or above it is stored pending_approval with no movements behind it, maker and checker must differ, approval applies the lines once through the same write the immediate path uses, a rejection needs a reason and moves nothing, and the history screen reads the whole life of the document off its own row. 04-42/04-43/04-45 (warehouse, its zones and bins, and the map) are built on the warehousing surface that already existed at /app/warehouses: a warehouse belongs to a branch and its code is unique there; the code may be renamed but the branch cannot change once the warehouse has moved stock, because stock is reported branch by branch, and a warehouse that has moved stock cannot be switched off or deleted at all because the ledger points at it; one default per branch is enforced in the service, so making a warehouse the default demotes the previous one. Zones carry a purpose (receiving/storage/picking/packing/dispatch/returns), bins live inside a zone and know their warehouse, and exactly one primary pick face per product per warehouse is enforced in the service (assigning a new one demotes the old). An empty zone is the only zone that can be removed and a bin with products still pointed at it cannot. The map is rendered from rows, and it names placements no movement has touched for 60 days. Bins record where, never how much: quantities stay in the ledger per product per warehouse.

06_suppliers.notes: Supplier master slice plus the money half. List with real KPIs and filters (06-01), create/update with duplicate name/BIN/phone refusal and a dedicated blacklist permission carrying a mandatory reason plus reinstatement (06-02), and a profile built from actual documents — outstanding delivery lines, recent orders/receipts, spend by month, and now what is owed with ageing buckets read from posted purchase bills (06-05, 06-09 partial). Partial: fixed category vocabulary (06-04), single contact and plain bank fields (06-06/06-07), payables on the profile but no company-wide due screen (06-09), spend without a report family (06-15). Payments against a supplier's bills are now real (06-10 partial, 03-47/03-52 own the mechanics) with a history filtered by supplier. Not started: import/export, a GL-derived supplier ledger and printable statement, supplier advances, contracts, performance scoring, documents. The supplier account is real (06-08, 06-09, 06-14): GET /app/suppliers/ledger lists every supplier the company has done money with (billed / paid / credited / still owed from three grouped aggregates), /app/suppliers/{id}/ledger is the running account (posted bills credit, payments and approved returns debit, one row per document with the balance after it, opening balance carried from before the range), /app/purchase/payables is the company-wide ageing with bucket filters, and /app/suppliers/{id}/statement is a printable document that also streams the same rows as CSV. Deviations stated: the ledger is document-derived rather than built from the AP control account's journal lines, and a supplier has no opening-balance field, so the account starts at the first document recorded.
